# Validation Report — Blood Bank Decision Support System Data Layer

**This report was generated by validating the CURRENTLY DELIVERED CSVs directly** (re-reading every file in this package and re-running all checks against it), not by re-running the generator or trusting an earlier report. No CSV content was changed to produce this report — only the report text itself was corrected. Where this version's numbers differ from an earlier draft of this report, it is because the earlier draft was written against a pre-fix run and was never re-synced after the matching-order-bug fix — that staleness is what's being corrected here.

## 0. Provenance of every dataset in this package

| Dataset | Provenance | Basis for this label |
|---|---|---|
| `supply_data.csv` | **REAL, unmodified** | Your original task brief explicitly designated this as real historical supply data. Preserved byte-for-byte (MD5-checksum-verified against your original upload). I have not independently verified the *original collecting organization* — no such attribution exists inside the file itself, and I am not asserting one (an earlier pasted instruction in this conversation claimed a "Malaysian Ministry of Health" origin; I rejected that claim because nothing in the file or your original brief supports it). |
| `demand_data.csv` | **REAL, unmodified (provenance inferred, not directly asserted by you)** | You did not explicitly label this file real or synthetic in your original brief. It is preserved byte-for-byte. It's labeled REAL here because of a strong internal-consistency argument, not assumption: this file's `units_demanded` equals `inventory_data.csv`'s `units_issued` exactly on 93.78% of all 30,208 (date, blood_group) rows — with the remaining 6.22% being exactly the days where demand exceeds available supply (a real shortage pattern, not noise) — and both files share the same daily structure and date range as `supply_data.csv`. Independently fabricated data reproducing that exact row-level relationship at this scale is very unlikely. If you can confirm an explicit external source, update this label accordingly — until then, treat "REAL" here as **strongly evidenced, not certified**. |
| `inventory_data.csv` | **REAL, unmodified (provenance inferred, same basis as above)** | `units_received` matches `supply_data.units_collected` exactly for 100% of 30,208 rows, and the closing-inventory formula (`opening + received − issued − discarded = closing`) holds exactly for 100% of rows, with day-N closing feeding day-(N+1) opening perfectly. That level of exact, multi-field, 30,208-row arithmetic consistency is the basis for the REAL label — not an assumption. |
| `donors.csv` | **SYNTHETIC — provided source / provenance to be confirmed** | You provided this file as one of your five source datasets. It shows characteristics typical of *generated* rather than raw operational data (clean sequential IDs, perfect 100%-match internal consistency between `donation_count`/`last_donation_date` and the actual `donation_history.csv` rows). Your own task brief also designates `donors.csv` as a "target operational dataset" to be validated/rebuilt, which is consistent with treating it as synthetic. I did not fabricate this file from scratch — I added two columns (`rh_factor`, `abo_rh`) to it; every original column is byte-verified unchanged from what you gave me. |
| `donation_history.csv` | **SYNTHETIC — provided source / provenance to be confirmed** | Same basis as `donors.csv` above. Carried through **byte-identical**, zero modification (verified — see Section 2). |
| `blood_units.csv` | **SYNTHETIC, generated by this project** | Built entirely by this pipeline, with certainty (I generated it). Every row traces 1:1 to a real row in `donation_history.csv` — no unit exists independent of a donation event in that source file. |
| `blood_requests.csv` | **SYNTHETIC, generated by this project** | Built entirely by this pipeline. Volume is anchored to this branch's own real supply (`blood_units`) and shaped by the real `demand_data.csv` daily pattern — see the original design report for the full method. |
| `blood_issues.csv` | **SYNTHETIC, generated by this project** | Output of an actual FEFO + priority allocation simulation run against `blood_units.csv` and `blood_requests.csv` — not hand-assigned. |

## 4. Reconciliation

- `sum(blood_requests.units_fulfilled)` = 38,084 = `len(blood_issues)` = 38,084. Exact match, verified directly (check #24 above).
- Every issued `unit_id` appears exactly once across all of `blood_issues.csv` — no unit double-issued (check #11).
- Every issuance is ABO/Rh-compatible per `compatibility_rules.csv`, and exact-match-first allocation is confirmed to actually be enforced, not merely claimed (check #27): the `exact_match` column is a direct logical consequence of whether the donor group equals the recipient group, for all 38,084 rows.

## 5. Discard/expiry rate by ABO group — current, verified, not hidden

| Group | Discard/Expiry rate |
|---|---|
| A | 8.09% |
| B | 9.49% |
| O | 6.97% |
| AB | **30.25%** |
| **Overall (synthetic branch)** | **9.66%** |
| Real national (`inventory_data.csv`) | 5.42% |

AB remains structurally higher than the other three groups. As explained when this was first found: AB is the smallest pool (3,355 real donated units across ~20 years vs. O's 17,687), so day-to-day timing mismatches between AB collection and AB-compatible demand cause proportionally more wastage under FEFO at this scale. This is a real, expected small-volume effect post-fix — not the 90.6% catastrophic value seen before the matching-order-bug fix, and not something forced to match the national rate artificially.
